Scope: arterial and local roads, potable water, sewage, storm drainage, irrigation, street lighting and telecom networks, sewage pump stations and storm drainage ponds for Phase 1, Part 2 of the 3rd Industrial City in Dammam.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours, on the same basis as last week: the 2,336,000 budgeted labour units of MODON's revised schedule, including engineering, procurement and testing. At the 24-Nov-2026 data date the project is 49.8% complete, up from 43.5% last week, against 68.6% planned, 18.8% behind plan. Almost all of this week's gain came from the delivery of the remaining 13 pumps; construction moved by only 0.3%.

The P6 update now finishes the project 183 days late. The contractor's P6 update (data date 21-Nov-2026) schedules project finish on 17-Nov-2027, 183 days after the contract completion date of 18-May-2027 and 7 days later than last week, with −182 days of float. MODON's revised schedule (update of 22-Nov-2026) now also finishes late, on 22-May-2027, and the weekly report still shows 18-May-2027. This week's gain of 6.32% is mostly procurement (5.98%); construction gained 0.30% and testing 0.04%, so the site works are not keeping pace: construction stands at 53.2% against 81.2% planned and testing at 31.1% against 55.6%. To finish on the contract date, the remaining 50.2% needs about 2.01% a week over the 25 whole weeks left.

Site photos this week

Six photos from this week's upload: four camera-stamped photos of 22 and 23 November 2026, and two cut from the contractor's daily site activity sheets of 18 and 22 November. Work covered installing the newly delivered pumps, flow testing of inspection manholes, uPVC pipe connections, kerbstones, backfilling around storm manholes and concrete encasement of the telecom ducts. The schedules uploaded this week disagree on completion. The contractor's P6 update (1,255 activities, data date 21-Nov-2026) finishes on 17-Nov-2027, 7 days later than last week's 10-Nov-2027; this time it records some progress (494 activities completed against 488). MODON's revised schedule, as reported in the Revised schedule sheet and the presentation (update of 22-Nov-2026), finishes on 22-May-2027, 4 days after the contract date, with procurement finishing on 24-Feb-2027, construction on 10-Apr-2027 and testing on 04-May-2027. The P6 export in the weekly report's Milestones sheet still shows 11-Jul-2027, and the weekly report itself forecasts 18-May-2027.

Procurement of key materials

Share of total quantity delivered to site for the long-lead items. Source: procurement log, Long Lead Procurement status sheet, and the weekly presentation, both updated this week.

Pumps: all 15 deliveredThe remaining 13 Grundfos pumps reached the project on 19-Nov-2026, so all 15 have now been delivered and are being installed at the stations in coordination with the consultant. Nothing else has reached site: the water station control panel (IGEC, 1 set) is expected in January 2027 and its delivery depends on settling the contractor's financial claim, and the sewage station panels (WAMCO, 4 sets) are expected from 24-Dec-2026 to the end of January 2027.
Generators and surge vessels still outstandingThe two generators (Kohler – Abunayyan) are in the Kingdom and wait for the factory and site acceptance tests. The VEGA generator parts are ready except the alternator, which has been shipped with no delivery date. The 7 surge vessels have been shipped from Egypt and are expected on site after customs on 03-Dec-2026, after a delay notified by the supplier. The water pump maintenance (SPP) is expected to start on 03-Dec-2026.

Open issues and risks

IssueOwnerDetail
Stoppages and permitsConsultant / MODONWorks were stopped from 07-Oct-2026 when the permit process changed without written notice to the contractor. Permits have since been approved: Road 1 on 25-Oct, Road 25 on 01-Nov (the stretch from the Road 2 junction to the Road 1 junction only from 22-Nov), Road 9 in Block F resumed on 21-Nov and Block F on 22-Nov-2026.
Road 25 crossingsContractor / MODONThe first part of the Road 25 / Road 2 crossing is done; the second part needs a traffic diversion approved by the city administration (target 03-Dec-2026). At Road 25 / Road 9, approval of pipe jacking for the sewer line is awaited.
Saudi Electricity permitsContractor / Consultant / MODONSaudi Electricity has suspended the remaining work permits, which directly delays handover of the works. Status: on hold; support from MODON and the consultant requested.
Sewer manholes clashing with the box culvertConsultant / MODONThe connections of 22 sewer manholes clash with the storm water box culvert. The contractor submitted a proposal on 14-Nov-2026 for the consultant's review (MODON issue log: critical).
Contractor's financial claimsConsultant / MODONThe consultant and MODON disagree over the contractor's claims (high risk). The contractor's letter DAM3-02-008-MAH-TS9-1-L-0199 of 16-Nov-2026 asks for a committee of MODON, the contractor and the Ministry of Finance to arbitrate; MODON's reply is awaited. Delivery of the water station control panel is tied to the claim.
Reduced contract valueMODONLess work can be executed because the contract value was reduced, lowering the contractor's expected cash flow (high risk). Action: study the project and the city's needs to fix the final scope.
Long-lead suppliesContractorControl panels, generators, surge vessels and pump maintenance parts are still to reach site because of regional and global shipping problems (high risk). Action: follow up purchase orders and deliveries.
Slab settlementConsultant / MODONA slab has settled because of works by WATCO and Al-Essa; several meetings have been held but Al-Essa's contractor has not responded (MODON issue log: high).
Office gate and lighting poleConsultantThe gate of the Al-Essa offices clashes with a lighting pole foundation; the consultant's direction is awaited.
Pond 4ContractorMODON approved the proposal; work starts after the sewer network at the Road 25 / Road 9 junction, and rain has delayed the surrounding works.
Network testingContractorThe testing plan was submitted with the recovery plan of 08-Nov-2026 and is to be updated weekly; testing stands at 31.1% against 55.6% planned.
Hand excavationContractorExcavation is done by hand because there are no records of the existing services, which lengthens the works. Action: trial pits before excavation.

Data notes

  • This-week values compare with the 17-Nov-2026 upload in the W08 folder (data date 15-Nov-2026), whose actual came from MODON's revised schedule MDD-Update 79 (1,015,605 of 2,336,000 budgeted labour units). That schedule file was not uploaded this week; this report takes plan and actual from the Revised schedule sheet ("Modon Revised - Update 22-11-26"), which matches slide 10 of the presentation: 1,163,326 earned and 1,602,701 planned units. The gain of 6.32% therefore spans more than one week of schedule data (MDD-Update 79 carried the data date 09-Nov-2026).
  • The report week is the contract week stated in the Milestones sheet ("Current Contract Weeks: 79 of 104"), which equals (24-Nov-2026 − 19-May-2025) ÷ 7 = 79 whole weeks. The workbook is report #67 in the General Information sheet.
  • The total row of the Revised schedule sheet gives 1,472,922 planned and 1,090,573 earned units, which leave out pre-testing and testing (129,778 and 72,753, entered one column to the right), while its percentages (68.61% and 49.80%) include them. This report uses the full figures.
  • The weekly plans are not on one basis: 56.0% at 08-Nov included pre-testing and testing, last week's 58.3% left them out, and this week's 68.6% includes them again, so the change in variance and SPI between weeks is partly a change of basis.
  • Of the 147,721 labour units gained, 139,804 are procurement (the remaining 13 pumps delivered on 19-Nov-2026); construction gained 6,960 and testing 957.
  • The Weekly Progress Report, Progress and Physical-Chart Data sheets are still on the old measure (construction man-hours only) and show 77.9% against 97.0% planned. In that sheet Local Roads shows 17,477 earned against 1,750 budgeted man-hours (999%), and Communications 0 earned.
  • The contractor's P6 update (data date 21-Nov-2026) records progress this week (33 activities changed, 6 completed) and finishes on 17-Nov-2027. It still leaves milestones 3 and 4 (work plan, drawings approval) not started, while the weekly report shows them complete. The Schedule sheet's activity counts (543 not started, 334 in progress, 378 completed) are unchanged from last week and do not match the P6 update (343, 418, 494).
  • Completion dates disagree: weekly report and presentation 18-May-2027; MODON revised update of 22-Nov-2026 22-May-2027; P6 export in the Milestones sheet 11-Jul-2027; contractor's P6 update 17-Nov-2027.
  • The earned value columns of the workbook, the cost table of the Revised schedule sheet and the financial slides of the presentation report value-weighted (cost-based) progress labelled as achieved; those figures are not used. The network percentages on slide 3 of the presentation have no stated basis (the testing figure matches the cost-based value) and are not used either.
  • Quantities in the presentation disagree between slides: storm pipes 48,963 m total and 47,633 m done on slide 11 against 47,638 m and 47,638 m on slide 12; potable water total 2,839 m against 2,992 m; telecom 21,318 m against 21,312 m. Two weeks ago the storm total was 42,617 m. The chamber valves are now listed apart from the chambers (0 of 59 and 0 of 70), where the 10-Nov presentation counted 44 and 55 chamber valves. The ponds are given as 9.71 of 10 ponds, against 0.93 of 11 two weeks ago.
  • Invoices: the weekly report and Invoice Log still show 14 progress invoices (65,141,130 SAR gross, last period to 30-Sep-2026), of which the summary counts 4 paid (15,540,346 SAR) and the log all 14. The presentation states 68,456,866 SAR paid up to invoice 15 of October 2026 after the 10% deduction (68,456,130 on slide 2) and 259,000 SAR of deductions. Invoice 8 is still shown paid on 01-Mar-2025, before its own period.
  • Contract value: the presentation uses 233,575,733 SAR and a saving of 69,405,562 SAR; the weekly report uses 233,776,077 SAR and the Revised schedule sheet a saving of 69,605,906 SAR.
  • Manpower: the monthly table is unchanged since the 10-Nov-2026 upload. The summary panel still shows 388 labour and 57 staff (445) against 332 and 66 (398) in the table and the presentation; equipment is 114 in the table and presentation and 72 in the Weekly Progress Report sheet.
  • The surge vessel delivery is 03-Dec-2026 in the procurement log and 28-Nov-2026 in the presentation's challenges table. The procurement log file name carries 10-24-2026 although it was updated this week.
  • The MODON issue log changed this week: the manpower and HSE issues were removed and the slab settlement, the Al-Essa gate clash and the 22 clashing sewer manholes added.
  • The "Modon PM" field in the weekly report is blank; the PM name is taken from the MODON risk and issue log.
